notes:
Summary: Orchid Genomics is a mid-size clinical genomics company evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) with an on-prem / air-gapped variant. Primary driver is regulatory+patient-data residency: clinical raw reads and derived data must never traverse public internet and must be retained with full audit trail for up to 7 years. They want a turnkey inference runtime that can operate in a disconnected datacenter and integrate with our KMS/HSM.

Key quotes: "No internet egress from inference nodes — period." — CTO. "Need cryptographic attestation for every image we run." — Head of IT.

Technical requirements (high-level):
- On-prem deployment delivered as validated OCI images + signed manifests; air-gapped installation media required.
- Integration with customer KMS/HSM (Thales + AWS KMS hybrid), ability to bring-your-own-keys and rotate keys without redeploying containers.
- Comprehensive audit logging per request: who/when/model/version, token-level cost attribution, immutable logs for 7+ years (WORM).
- Data residency: all storage in US-owned datacenter; no backups to external regions unless explicitly allowed.
- Network controls: strict egress firewall rules, optional egress-proxy for package updates via vetted mirror.
- Patch / upgrade process must support offline bundle installation and signed rollbacks.
- Ability to lock model weights on-prem with hardware attestation; prohibition on exporting proprietary weights.

POC scope requested:
- 3-week on-prem POC in their Boston colo: install + smoke tests + 1 sample pipeline (variant-annotation assistant) using a 2-node GPU pool.
- Latency/throughput targets: P95 latency < 250ms for short clinical prompts (~200 tokens), sustained throughput ~500 reqs/day for batch analysis.
- Security verification: run through Redwood security questionnaire, provide container SBOMs, cryptographic signatures, attestations, and SOC2/ISO docs.

Recent timeline (selected):
- 2025-11-12: Lead created after intro at BioData Summit (Sofia).
- 2025-11-20: Intro demo (hosted) — positive for latency & API ergonomics.
- 2025-12-05: Security questionnaire sent by Orchid; they returned preliminary responses 2025-12-18.
- 2026-01-08: Deep-dive with Infra + Security (Fireflies ff_2026_01_08_orchid_intro) — discussed air-gapped installer semantics.
- 2026-02-10: Follow-up with SE to scope HSM integration (Fireflies ff_2026_02_10_secqa_call).
- 2026-02-22: Pricing deck shared (/drive/pricing/orchid-pricing-deck-v3.pdf) and legal handed DPA for review.

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal needs explicit data residency language for derived embeddings and logs (DPA markups expected).
- Orchid insists on offline attestation flow for upgrades; need to confirm Redwood support for signed offline upgrade bundles.
- KMS/HSM playbook: they use Thales + occasional AWS KMS in hybrid mode — confirm HSM agent and rotation APIs.

Sales notes / risks:
- High enterprise ARR but long procurement cycle due to legal/infrastructure signoffs.
- Good fit for Redwood Private; potential to expand to Dedicated for less sensitive workloads.
- Security team is pragmatic but strict — provide crisp runbook, glossaries, and a one-page air-gapped install plan to unblock.

Next steps (short):
- Action: SE (Liam) to produce a 1-page air-gap install and upgrade runbook draft by 2026-03-05.
- Action: Send signed SBOM sample and attestation examples; attach to security FAQ doc.
- Legal: Redwood legal to review DPA markups by 2026-03-12.

Stubs / references: DPA draft link: /drive/legal/orchid-dpa-draft-2026.docx, Jira: INF-312 for install script work, SEC-2041 for HSM integration.
